title: Amazing grace (Newton, 1779)
hookLine: 'twas grace that taught my heart to fear, and grace my fears relieved
tomorrow: a song asks you straight out: were you there when…?

cards: The end-of-year slideshow: freshman photos, bad haircuts, the trip, the hard semester, and then a final slide that just says what's next. Looking back and looking ahead in one breath.
A hymn printed in Olney Hymns under the title Faith's Review and Expectation does exactly that. You know it by its first two words: amazing grace.

teach.b: John Newton wrote it, and the title is a map. The review comes first: "I once was lost, but now am found, Was blind, but now I see."

teach.h: GRACE TAUGHT FEAR, THEN RELIEVED IT.
teach.b: Then a line that surprises people: "'Twas grace that taught my heart to fear, And grace my fears reliev'd." The same grace does both: first it shows you where you really stand, then it calms you there.
Then the expectation: "Thro' many dangers, toils and snares, I have already come; 'Tis grace has brought me safe thus far, And grace will lead me home." Thus far is a Bible word in disguise.
Newton set the hymn beside King David's prayer: "Who am I, O LORD God, and what is mine house, that thou hast brought me hitherto?"
So the hymn is David's question, sung: look how far I've been brought, and the same hands will bring me the rest of the way.

how: Amazing Grace is sung in churches of many kinds, at funerals and at gatherings far beyond church; it first appeared in Newton and Cowper's Olney Hymns.

o: a prayer of thanks said over the meal at a church supper
a song sailors sang to keep time while they hauled rope
Newton's hymn looking back on grace and ahead to home

games.q: review and expectation — tap the pairs.
p: grace taught my heart to fear

s: 'twas grace that taught my heart to fear, and grace my fears relieved: the same grace does both.
Newton set the hymn beside King David's prayer in 1 Chronicles
who am I ... that thou hast brought me hitherto? hitherto is thus far.
the hymn only looks back at the past
its old title is Faith's Review and Expectation: back over the road, and ahead to home.

games.q: your grandma says she's 'too far gone' for church after years away. which line from Newton's hymn speaks most directly to her?
o: I once was lost, but now am found.
grace taught my heart to fear: she should be afraid.
none: the hymn is for people who never left.
games.why: the hymn starts with lost and found, and its next move is grace calming the fear it uncovered.

practice: Sing one verse, out loud or under your breath, any tune you know: 'tis grace has brought me safe thus far, and grace will lead me home. If singing isn't yours, say it slowly instead.
Then sit with the two halves: how far you've come, and where you're headed.

wordCard.voice: Amazing grace. Newton's hymn of review and expectation: lost and found, fear taught and relieved, and a road that ends at home.

orig.note: Greek: grace, gift, favor. the New Testament word behind the hymn's first word.

carryVoice: Your line: grace will lead me home. Thus far, and the rest of the way. Two weeks, sung through.
